structure: Part 13 read in full: private-transporter-details/ (controller.js 220 lines, .njk 103 lines), commercial-transporter-details/ (controller.js 208 lines, .njk 131 lines), transporter-details-save.js (118 lines), fit/commercial-transporter-details.fit.spec.js (365 lines, every test), fit/transporters.fit.spec.js (1508 lines, read in full; only its tests about the two details forms are claimed, the list, search and type-question tests are part 12's), and copy/copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (only the privateTransporterDetails and commercialTransporterDetails keys, plus the transporters.guidance keys the commercial form shows). The *.test.js unit tests were left out as the partition says. page.js, own-transporter-type.js, transporter-add-session.js, services/countries/index.js, services/transporters/commercial-country.js and shared/kit.js were opened for provenance only. It covers two pages: the private form at transporters/add/private (name, two address lines, town, county, postcode, a country select of the United Kingdom plus every reference-data country, email, phone) and the commercial form at transporters/add/commercial (authorisation number first, the same address and contact fields, a disabled country fixed to Northern Ireland, and an Important banner of authorisation guidance); every required and length rule with its message; the entry guard; what a save writes to the notification and the address book and where it lands; cancel; the recoverable-error path; remembering a refused attempt; Welsh parity; and what the two fit specs prove, accessibility included.

claims.statement: The private transporter details form is reached by answering Private on the transporter type question, and is served at /notifications/<journeyId>/transporters/add/private, carrying the trail the trader arrived with.
claims.note: The slug 'transporters/add/private' is set in page.js:31-35, outside this part's read list, opened for provenance; the controller registers its GET and POST through kit.pageRoutes(page, { get, post }).

claims.statement: The commercial transporter details form is reached by answering Commercial on the transporter type question, and is served at /notifications/<journeyId>/transporters/add/commercial, carrying the trail the trader arrived with.
claims.note: The slug 'transporters/add/commercial' is set in page.js:25-29, outside this part's read list, opened for provenance.

claims.statement: Both transporter details pages are marked as agreed behaviour, the maturity level that makes a page signed off.
claims.note: page.js is outside this part's read list and was opened for provenance only. A change to either page's behaviour trips the build loop's signed-off check.

claims.note: The caption's words live in the flow's section-captions copy, which belongs to another part; this claim records only that these two pages show that caption.

The back link on each details page goes to the transporter type question, carrying the trail the trader arrived with.

The private form asks for the name, the address and the contact details in the order name or organisation name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode, country, email address, phone number.
The commercial form asks the transporter authorisation number first, before the name, and then takes the same address and contact fields in the same order as the private form.

claims.statement: Both details forms are offered in Welsh, with a Welsh value for every key the English file holds, including the fixed country, which reads "Gogledd Iwerddon".
claims.note: Read for key parity rather than string by string, as the partition says. The one key whose Welsh and English differ in shape is countryRequired, which in both files points at that file's own SELECT_A_COUNTRY constant: 'Select a country' in English, 'Dewiswch wlad' in Welsh.

claims.statement: The Welsh copy for both details forms is machine-drafted and has not been reviewed by a translator, so it is not fit to ship to users as it stands.

claims.statement: The private form's fields are checked against reference data on every submission, so the list of countries it will accept is whatever reference data serves at that moment rather than what was offered when the page was drawn.
claims.note: It follows because the private controller builds its rules inside an async fields() called per request, where the commercial controller composes its rules once at module scope; only the private form needs a live list.

claims.statement: The commercial form does not offer an alternative to the authorisation number: a commercial transporter cannot be added without one.
The private form asks for no authorisation number at all.

claims.note: It follows because the only successful exit from either form is the redirect to the transporters slug, and the fit tests then click the list's own save control to reach the overview.

claims.statement: A save writes the transporter onto the notification before it creates the address book record, so when the address book save fails the notification can already hold the new transporter while the form shows the recoverable error.
claims.note: mechanism: orders the notification commit and the address book write inside one recoverable save. It follows because state.commit runs before saveTransporterToAddressBook, and the failure branch only clears the just-added name; it does not undo the commit. No fit test exercises this.

claims.statement: Saving one type of transporter writes only that type's record and the type itself, leaving any record of the other type already on the notification in place.
claims.note: mechanism: works on the privateTransporter and commercialTransporter answers. It follows because each form's record patch names only its own key; transporterType says which one applies.

claims.statement: The commercial form makes no check on opening that a saved country is still available, unlike the private form, because its country is always Northern Ireland.
claims.note: It follows because the commercial GET renders with no errors, and its copy holds no countryNoLongerAvailable message.
